# papercut-explainer: notes for coding agents

This repo makes short vertical explainer reels that look like layered construction paper. It is nine Agent Skills plus a
Remotion library. If your harness loads skills from `.agents/skills` or `skills/` (most do), they are already available here.
If it does not, read the matching `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` yourself when a request fits its description.

| Skill | Use it when the user wants to |
|---|---|
| `papercut-explainer` | make a reel end to end, or does not say which stage; it routes to the rest |
| `papercut-strategy` | decide what the reel should be: topic, format, audience, funnel, competitor study |
| `papercut-hook` | write or fix the hook (five scored variants, frame-0 cover) |
| `papercut-script` | turn a link into a researched script (75-95 words on a fixed spine) |
| `papercut-storyboard` | storyboard a script: camera and cut table, scene by scene, before any code |
| `papercut-voice` | voice the reel and time it to the picture |
| `papercut-build` | build and render the episode from a storyboard with the library |
| `papercut-qa` | check stills and the cut against the style and the storyboard |
| `papercut-setup` | install or repair this repo's setup (`./install.sh --doctor` first) |

- Library path: `$PAPERCUT_LIB`, else `PAPERCUT_LIB=` in `~/.config/papercut-explainer/config.env`, else `./library` here.
- Each skill reads the files the stage before it wrote, so you can stop after any stage.
- Scene-building agent: `papercut-scene` (installed per harness by `install.sh`). With no subagent support, build the scenes yourself, one at a time.
- Aider and other agents without skills support: `aider --read AGENTS.md`, then read the `SKILL.md` that fits.
- Harness folders and models: `harnesses.sh` and the README's *Works with* section.

# Prompts

Copy-paste prompts for each skill, in the order of the workflow, with what to expect. Replace anything in `<angle brackets>`.

Your agent picks a skill from your wording. If the wrong one loads, or none does, name it: "use papercut-hook to write 5 hooks for this fact list". Each skill reads the files the stage before it wrote, so you can stop after any stage and pick up in a new session. `examples/paper-trail/` shows what every stage writes.

## End to end

```
Make a papercut explainer about <link>, 25 seconds, CTA keyword PAPER
```

- Loads `papercut-explainer`, the router. It checks your install mode, finds `$PAPERCUT_LIB` and your series folder, then asks which run mode you want (full reel, script only, storyboard from a script, style prompt, fix one scene).
- Asks only what is missing: the claim the video proves, who does the work in the product (role framing), what the viewer gets for the keyword, and the audience level if there is no `SERIES.md`.
- Writes the BRIEF at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/research/facts.md`, then hands to `papercut-strategy` and walks the stages. It renders only when you ask.

Other ways in:

```
Write only the script, banners and staging table for <link>. No video yet.
Storyboard this script: <path to narration/script.json>
Give me the papercut style prompt for <image or video tool>
```

These pick the "script only", "storyboard from an existing script" and "style prompt" run modes. The last one hands you a block from `references/style-prompt.md` and stops.

## 1. Setup

```
Set up papercut-explainer, partial install
```

- Loads `papercut-setup`. It runs `./install.sh --doctor` from the repo root and tells you in plain words what is installed and which mode that adds up to.
- Asks, in one question: how much (Minimal, Standard, Full or Custom), skills for every project or one, symlink or copy. "Partial" usually means Minimal, or Custom with the components you name (`skills,deps,pytools,verify`). It asks again before any multi-GB download.
- Runs `install.sh --yes` with the matching flags and writes `~/.config/papercut-explainer/config.env`, which every later skill reads for the library path. A new Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI session picks up the linked skills (restart it); opencode reloads them automatically.

## 2. Strategy

```
Pick the topic, format and funnel for a reel about <link>. Audience: <who>.
```

- Loads `papercut-strategy`. It reads `SERIES.md` first, and if there is none it asks for the audience (who, level, regions), voice, palette, mascot and keyword log, then writes it.
- Picks the one familiar format for the whole reel ("what show is this secretly about?"), the mode, the keyword and the freebie, and plans the caption.
- Writes `SERIES.md` and the BRIEF block at the top of `research/facts.md`. Next stage: the hook.

The same skill also runs competitor studies and the post-publish autopsy:

```
Study these 4 reels and tell me what to borrow: <url> <url> <url> <url>
Here are the numbers for the reel I posted: <views, skip rate, watch time, comments>. Do the autopsy.
```

The first spawns one subagent per reel and saves `research/analytics/YYYY-MM-DD-<creator>-reels.md`. The second reads the numbers hook first, topic second, and writes `research/analytics/YYYY-MM-DD-autopsy.md` plus an update to `SERIES.md`.

## 3. Hook

```
Write 5 hooks for this fact list: <paste the facts, or point at research/facts.md>
```

- Loads `papercut-hook`. It needs the BRIEF. If there is none it sends you to `papercut-strategy`.
- Writes five variants from at least three hook patterns, scores each on the six-question hook check, drops any that fail the facts, and picks the best.
- Writes the HOOK block (SAY, WRITE, SHOW, ALIGN) at the top of `papercut/STORYBOARD.md`. The WRITE line becomes the `hook` title in `episode.json` when `papercut-build` fills it in. It also sets the rule for the motion out of the hook, which the storyboard applies.

## 4. Script

```
Write the script, banner track and staging table for <link>
```

- Loads `papercut-script`. It needs the BRIEF and the HOOK block. It researches the source (web fetch or search, a browser for screenshots) and asks you for screenshots and facts if it has none of those.
- Writes the sourced facts list under the BRIEF in `research/facts.md`, the 75-95 word script on the 10-beat spine in `narration/script.json` (line `l1_hook` is the SAY line), 10-18 banners, and a staging table with one set per banner and a GAG column from the humour pass.
- The staging table goes into `papercut/STORYBOARD.md` under the HOOK block. Stressed words per line are marked there for the voice stage.

## 5. Storyboard

```
Storyboard this script
```

- Loads `papercut-storyboard`. It needs `narration/script.json` and the HOOK block and staging table. It reads the two library catalogs to check every camera move, cut kind, backdrop and SFX name.
- Writes the global rules, the Camera / Cut table (one row per scene, no plain `CameraPush` on more than a third), one block per scene with an event on each stressed word, and the SFX plan into `papercut/STORYBOARD.md`.
- The cut column becomes `cuts` in `episode.json` at the next stage. The Timing section is left for the voice stage.

## 6. Voice

Three paths. Say which one, or the skill asks.

**A. Local Qwen3-TTS** (Full install)

```
Voice the episode with local Qwen3-TTS, speaker Ryan
```

- Loads `papercut-voice`. It checks that `qwen_tts` imports and hands to `papercut-setup` if not. It copies `voice.example.json` to `voice/voice.json` and sets the speaker and the style line (`instruct`).
- Plays the first three lines before the full run, then generates takes, picks one per line and writes `voice/final_narrator/<id>.wav` and `timing_narrator.js`.
- Finishes with `build_vo.py` and `timing_md.py`: `public/vo/captions.json`, `src/plan.json` and the Timing section of `STORYBOARD.md`.

**B. Your own recording or another TTS**

```
I recorded the narration myself, one file per line, in <folder>. Time the script to it.
```

- Loads `papercut-voice`, path B. It needs an ASR backend (mlx-whisper or faster-whisper) for word times, and asks for one WAV per line or raw takes.
- Writes `voice/final_narrator/`, the ASR file and `timing_narrator.js`, then the same captions, plan and Timing section.
- Without ASR it can only estimate 2.75 words a second, and says that captions will drift.

**C. Placeholder voice**

```
Use a placeholder voice so I can see the timing
```

- Loads `papercut-voice`, path C (Standard install). It runs `placeholder_vo.py` from `narration/` with a pace of 3.5 to 4 words a second, silent or the macOS `say` voice.
- Writes silent WAVs and `timing_narrator.js`, then runs `build_vo.py`, which flags any scene under 1.2 s. You can build, preview and QA the whole reel, and re-voice later without touching a scene.

## 7. Build

```
Build scenes S03-S06 with parallel scene agents
```

- Loads `papercut-build` (and the Remotion best-practices skill). It needs `papercut/STORYBOARD.md` and `src/plan.json`. It builds `S01Hook` itself first, as the reference scene.
- Splits S03 to S06 across scene agents, two or three scenes each, and gives each the project path, its frame ranges, a QA folder and `library/papercut/AGENT_BRIEF.md`. Each agent writes only `src/scenes/<Scene>.tsx` and `tools/cue_sheet.d/<Scene>.json`.
- Agents QA their own stills. You get a short report per agent. Nothing renders unless you ask.

Other build requests:

```
Scaffold the episode as 01-<slug> in <series folder>
Mix the sound for the episode
Render it
```

They run `new_episode.sh` (and merge your earlier files into the new folder), then `cues.py` with `audio/render.mjs`, then `render.sh` for `out/<name>.mp4`.

## 8. QA

```
QA the reel
```

- Loads `papercut-qa`. It renders contact sheets with `qa.sh`, four to six frames per scene, one render at a time.
- Checks them against the style checklist and the storyboard: paper look, banner rules, the HOOK block on screen, a camera move in every scene, humour pass, bottom 20% clear.
- Fixes go back to `papercut-build`, at most two rounds per scene. The last step is a delivery summary that names what is still placeholder (voice, music, SFX, assets).

## Maintenance

**Re-voice with a different speaker**

```
Re-voice the episode with a different speaker
```

Loads `papercut-voice`. It asks which speaker (Aiden is the other recommended one), changes `speaker` in `voice/voice.json`, regenerates the takes, finalizes them, then reruns `build_vo.py` and `timing_md.py`. Scene starts move with the new word times, and the scene cache re-renders everything.

**Swap the mascot's colour**

```
Swap the mascot's colour to <colour>
```

Loads `papercut-build`. Say whether the colour is for this episode or the whole series. For one episode it changes the `color` and `shade` props the scenes pass to the `Critter`, and only those scenes re-render. For the series it changes the hero colour in the library's `kit/tokens.ts`, re-syncs with `sync_kit.sh` (a kit change re-renders everything) and notes the colour in `SERIES.md`. It never edits `src/lib/` inside a project, because that folder is a synced copy.

**Add a backdrop**

```
Add a backdrop for <place>
```

Loads `papercut-build`. It checks the 24 existing sets first, and generates or draws a new one only if none fits (an image tool, or code like `backdrops-src/`). The JPG goes in `library/papercut/public/bg/backdrops/`, with an entry in `backdrops.json` and the `BACKDROPS` table in `kit/paper/backdrops.tsx`. Then it runs `tools/catalog.py` and `sync_kit.sh`.

**Add a sound effect**

```
Add a sound effect: <describe it>
```

Loads `papercut-build`. It writes `library/audio/sfx/<name>.js` with the `// @sfx name | tags | seconds | description | origin` header line, runs `tools/catalog.py` so it shows in `audio/CATALOG.md`, and adds a row to the scene's `tools/cue_sheet.d/<Scene>.json`. Then `cues.py` and `render.mjs` rebuild the audio.

**Fix scene S04 so the camera moves**

```
Fix scene S04 so the camera moves
```

Loads `papercut-explainer` (run mode "fix one scene"), which hands to `papercut-build` and then `papercut-qa`. It reads S04's row in the Camera / Cut table. If the table names no camera move for S04, run `papercut-storyboard` first to choose one. Then it edits `src/scenes/S04*.tsx` to use that move, checks the scene with `qa.sh`, and re-renders only that scene.

# Papercut build

Build every episode on the library instead of writing a Remotion project from scratch. Read `library/README.md` once.

## Preflight

- Install: **Standard** or Full. Needs the library, node 20+, npm, ffmpeg, Python tools (numpy, Pillow, soundfile) and Chrome or Chromium for the audio render. Probe with the commands in `papercut-explainer`; if something is missing, run `./install.sh --doctor` and hand over to `papercut-setup`.
- Library: `$PAPERCUT_LIB`, else the `PAPERCUT_LIB=` line in `~/.config/papercut-explainer/config.env`, else ask once. With no library at all, build from the sketches in `../papercut-explainer/references/remotion-recipes.md`.
- Load the Remotion best-practices skill first (`remotion-best-practices`, from the Remotion plugin, or `npx skills add remotion-dev/skills -g -y -a <your harness id>`; `install.sh --mode standard` does this) and follow its routing for markup, captions and the Studio.
- Needs `papercut/STORYBOARD.md` and `narration/script.json` from the earlier stages.
- Smoke test of the whole toolchain: `library/tools/selftest.sh` builds `examples/hello-reel/` in a throwaway folder and renders one still.

## 1. Scaffold

```
$PAPERCUT_LIB/new_episode.sh <series-dir> NN-slug CompId [out-name]
```

It creates `<series>/episodes/NN-slug/{research,narration/voice,papercut}` with the template project and a synced copy of the kit in `src/lib/`. `node_modules` comes from `$DONOR`, else the newest sibling episode, else `npm i`. If `<series>/papercut-assets/` exists, it is laid over the default textures and props.

The folder may already exist, because the earlier stages wrote `research/`, `narration/script.json` and `papercut/STORYBOARD.md` into it. The script merges into it and never overwrites a file that is there. It stops only if `papercut/package.json` exists (already scaffolded).

Never edit `src/lib/` in a project. It is a snapshot, so an old episode renders the same after the library changes. Fix the library, then re-sync with `papercut/sync_kit.sh`.

## 2. Plan: `episode.json`, voice, timing

From the storyboard, fill `papercut/episode.json`:
- `scenes`: `[["S01Hook", "l1_hook", 0], ["S02Name", "l2_name", "called"], ...]` (scene id, narration line id, first word as an index or the exact word).
- `banners`: `{"S01Hook": "TAKEAWAY IN CAPS"}`. `hook`: see `papercut-hook`. `cuts`: the Camera / Cut table's cut column. `bed`, `whipScene`, `cutSfx`, `gaps` (extra beat after a line, in seconds).

Then run `papercut-voice` through its timing step (it ends with `build_vo.py` and `timing_md.py`). Then, from `papercut/`:

```
python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/papercut/stubs.py        # src/scenes/index.ts + a stub per scene
```

`build_vo.py` flags any scene under 1.2 s; merge it into a neighbour. `timing_md.py` writes the Timing section of `STORYBOARD.md` (absolute frames and word cues), so agents never open `plan.json`.

## 3. Assets

Follow `../papercut-explainer/references/asset-prompts.md`: an image tool (anything that outputs transparent PNGs) for backgrounds and complex static props, code for characters, all text, tags, gauges, buttons and UI. No text inside generated images. With no image tool, build every prop in code with the paper filter; the style holds up. Backdrops: use the library's `<Backdrop>` set (`library/papercut/public/bg/backdrops/_sheet.jpg`); generate a new one only when an episode needs a place the library lacks. The proof screenshot: `node $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/capture.mjs <url> public/proof/x.png`, shown with the kit's `RealShot`.

## 4. Scenes

1. Build `S01Hook` yourself first, from the HOOK block. It is the reference scene the agents match (cue constants, the camera, clamped `interpolate`).
2. Hand the rest to scene agents in parallel, grouped by scene (2-3 scenes each; more agents cost more startup context). Use the `papercut-scene` agent that `install.sh` wrote for your harness (Claude Code `~/.claude/agents`, OpenCode `~/.config/opencode/agents`, Codex `~/.codex/agents`, Gemini CLI `~/.gemini/agents`); a general agent also works. Spawn it with your harness's own mechanism (the Task tool in Claude Code, the subagent tool in opencode, Codex's subagents, Gemini's agent tool). **If your harness has no subagents, build the scenes yourself one at a time**, in the same order and with the same brief; it is slower, not different. The brief is `library/papercut/AGENT_BRIEF.md`. The spawn message gives the project path, each agent's scenes with absolute frame ranges, a QA folder name and the value of `$PAPERCUT_LIB`.
3. File ownership: an agent writes only `src/scenes/<Scene>.tsx`, an optional `<Scene>.parts.tsx` and `tools/cue_sheet.d/<Scene>.json`. Never `src/lib/**`, other scenes, `index.ts`, `plan.json`, `episode.json` or the storyboard.
4. Agents read `library/papercut/CATALOG.md` and `library/audio/CATALOG.md`, not the kit source, and reuse components, prop sets and scene templates (`kit/scenes/`, for example `CtaPhoneDM` for the CTA) before drawing anything new.

Build rules: 1080x1920, 30 fps, scenes chained in the kit's transition series. Global layers: VO and music `<Audio>`, the taped banner with `<Boil>`, `<WordTagCaptions>`, `<GrainOverlay>`. Every prop is wrapped in `<Paper>`, entrances use `<PopIn>`, each scene runs inside its storyboard camera. No CSS animations. Keep the bottom 20% clear. Neighbouring scenes never share a backdrop. The default hero is a boxy orange critter (token `C.hero` `#D67354`, shade `C.heroLo` `#A9553B`, alias `you`); accessories and name pills tell the cast apart.

## 5. Sound

Pick SFX by name from `library/audio/sfx/*.js` and the bed by preset from `library/audio/beds/*.json`. From `papercut/`:

```
python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/cues.py && node $PAPERCUT_LIB/audio/render.mjs
```

`cues.py` merges the agents' rows into `tools/cues.json` and prints a note if air sounds exceed one per 2.5 s. `render.mjs` writes `public/audio/music.wav` and `fx.wav`.

## 6. Render

Preview in the Studio (`npx remotion studio`). Render only when asked:

```
$PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/render.sh        # -> out/<out>.mp4
```

Flags: `--workers N` (default 3), `--conc N`, `--force`, `--keep`. Each scene is cached, so after a fix only the changed scene re-renders; a change to the kit, plan, voice or captions re-renders everything. The first run downloads Remotion's headless Chrome, and `out/cache` takes several GB of ProRes.

To fix or rebuild one scene: edit `src/scenes/<Scene>.tsx`, check it with `papercut-qa`, then run `render.sh` again.

## 7. Harvest (after the episode)

```
python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/harvest.py .       # from papercut/; read-only report
python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/catalog.py         # regenerate both catalogs
```

Promote kit fixes, reusable components, new SFX and recurring beats as `library/HARVEST.md` describes, and add an entry to `library/CHANGELOG.md`.

- When a move looks stiff or muddy, check `../papercut-explainer/references/motion-principles.md` for the matching principle and its kit helper.

## Hand-off

Next is `papercut-qa`, which reads stills from the project and `STORYBOARD.md`. Run it per scene while building and once on the whole reel before the final render. After posting, `papercut-strategy` runs the autopsy.

# Papercut Explainer

A ~20-45 s vertical explainer that looks like layered construction paper brought to life: grainy paper props with drop shadows, rigid cut-out animation, a slow camera push with stop-motion paper boil, a taped headline banner per beat and word-by-word torn-paper caption tags. Built with Remotion, optional AI-generated textured assets, and any TTS.

Every beat runs three tracks:
- the voiceover tells the story
- the taped banner adds a hard fact the voiceover skips
- a fresh paper set illustrates the voiceover's words, with a rough papercut rebuild of the product UI doing the demo

Reuse the style and the storytelling, not the worked examples' content. Every product, company and number in the examples is invented. The style rules are in `references/style-guide.md` (section 2 is the Style DNA).

## Preflight

- **Library.** Resolve `$PAPERCUT_LIB`, else the `PAPERCUT_LIB=` line in `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/papercut-explainer/config.env`, else ask once. Never hard-code a machine path. Stages 1 to 4 need no library.
- **Install mode.** Probe it before promising a stage (see Install modes below).
- **Series.** Find the series folder (it holds `episodes/`). Read its `SERIES.md` if it exists.

## Run modes (ask first)

1. **Full reel**, idea to mp4: stages 1 to 8, then stage 9 after posting.
2. **Script only**: strategy, hook, script (stop after the staging table).
3. **Storyboard from an existing script**: `papercut-storyboard`. Ask for the script, the facts and the HOOK block.
4. **Style prompt for another tool**: give the right block from `references/style-prompt.md` and stop.
5. **Fix or rebuild one scene**: `papercut-build` (scenes step), then `papercut-qa`.

## Intake (ask only what is missing)

- **Source**: usually a link (repo, product site, announcement). Everything else is researched from it.
- **The one claim** the video proves, and the topic.
- **Role framing**: who or what does the work, who advises or approves. Confirm it with the user and never invent product behaviour.
- **CTA keyword** and what the viewer gets (the deliverable).
- **Length**: default 22-30 s.
- **Audience level** (from `SERIES.md`) and any accent colour or mascot.

Write the answers as the BRIEF block at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/research/facts.md` (format in `papercut-strategy`).

## Stages

| # | Stage | Skill | Reads | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Strategy | `papercut-strategy` | `SERIES.md`, the source | BRIEF in `research/facts.md`, `SERIES.md` |
| 2 | Hook | `papercut-hook` | BRIEF | HOOK block at the top of `papercut/STORYBOARD.md` |
| 3 | Script | `papercut-script` | BRIEF, HOOK | `research/facts.md`, `narration/script.json`, staging table in `STORYBOARD.md` |
| 4 | Storyboard | `papercut-storyboard` | `script.json`, `STORYBOARD.md` | Camera/Cut table, scene blocks, SFX plan in `STORYBOARD.md` |
| 5 | Scaffold and plan | `papercut-build` | `STORYBOARD.md` | the project, `episode.json` |
| 6 | Voice and timing | `papercut-voice` | `script.json`, `voice/voice.json` | `narration/` takes, `public/vo/captions.json`, `src/plan.json` |
| 7 | Scenes, sound, render | `papercut-build` | `plan.json`, `STORYBOARD.md` | `src/scenes/*`, `tools/cues.json`, `out/*.mp4` |
| 8 | QA | `papercut-qa` | stills, `STORYBOARD.md` | fixes, the delivery summary |
| 9 | After posting | `papercut-strategy` (autopsy), `papercut-build` (harvest) | platform numbers, the project | `research/analytics/`, library promotions |

## Project files

The pipeline lives in files, not in chat. Each stage reads the files above and writes its own, so a new session can resume from any stage.

```
<series>/
  SERIES.md                  optional: audience, voice, palette, mascot, keyword log
  voice/voice.json           optional: voice settings (copy library/voice/voice.example.json)
  papercut-assets/           optional: overlay textures and props
  research/analytics/        optional: competitor studies and autopsies
  episodes/NN-slug/
    research/facts.md        BRIEF + facts with sources
    narration/script.json    [{"id": "l1_hook", "text": "..."}, ...]
    papercut/
      episode.json           scenes, banners, hook, gaps, bed, cuts
      STORYBOARD.md          HOOK, staging table, Camera/Cut table, scene blocks
```

Library catalogs: `library/papercut/CATALOG.md` (every kit component) and `library/audio/CATALOG.md` (every SFX and bed). They are generated, so a fresh checkout may lack them or have stale ones. Run `python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/catalog.py` to rebuild. Agents read the catalogs, not the kit source.

Reuse before writing: a kit component, a props set or a scene template beats new drawing code. Pick SFX and beds by name.

## Install modes

- **Minimal** (skills only): strategy, hook, script, storyboard, style prompts. No rendering.
- **Standard**: Minimal + build and render with a placeholder voice (silent, or macOS `say`) via `library/tools/placeholder_vo.py`, stills QA, SFX and bed audio, the full mp4.
- **Full**: Standard + local Qwen3-TTS voiceover and word-timed captions from real audio.

Probe (read-only):

```
. "$(grep '^PAPERCUT_LIB=' "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/papercut-explainer/config.env" | cut -d= -f2-)/env.sh"   # fills PAPERCUT_PY, QWEN_TTS_PY
node -v; ffmpeg -version | head -1
"$PAPERCUT_PY" -c 'import numpy, PIL, soundfile'
"$QWEN_TTS_PY" -c 'import qwen_tts'
```

The first three lines passing means Standard. The `qwen_tts` import passing as well means Full. If a stage needs more than the install provides, say so in one line, run `./install.sh --doctor` from the repo root, and hand over to `papercut-setup` instead of improvising. # Papercut hook

The hook is the most important step. A reel's hook is three separate, explicit layers, and none may be skipped or left implied. Write all of them before anything else in the script.

## Preflight

- Install: Minimal is enough. No library needed.
- Read the BRIEF at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/research/facts.md` (topic, format, audience, CTA) and the facts list, so every claim can be checked. If there is no BRIEF, run `papercut-strategy` first.
- Read `SERIES.md` for the audience level and regions.

## The HOOK block

```
HOOK
SAY:   <the first spoken sentence>
WRITE: <the frame-0 title, 2-5 words, ideally a number; the episode.json "hook">
SHOW:  <what frame 0 and the first 2 s show: the mid-action moment, the camera move>
ALIGN: <the one idea all three point at>
```

No scene gets built until all four lines are filled and pass the alignment test.

| Layer | Rule |
|---|---|
| SHOW, the first frame | The most striking moment, already mid-action. No establishing shot, no fade-in, no empty room. It must make sense muted. |
| WRITE, the on-screen title | The cover title (2-5 words, ideally a number), fully visible on frame 0 for about 2-3 s. It carries the other half of the gap, never the same words as the voice. |
| SAY, the spoken line | Opens the gap within about 10 words. Names who it's for. The stake or number comes early. Never answers itself. No anonymous news framing ("Someone just released..."); a named, credible source is fine. |

Skip the "stated as news" opening from beat 1 of the spine ("A solo dev just open-sourced..."). Open the gap and the stake instead, and name a big brand the viewer already knows in the first sentence.

## Alignment test

What you show, what you write and what you say all point at one idea. They differ in words, never in subject. If the voice says "your screenshots leaked" while frame 0 is a calm desk and the title is about stars, each layer opens a different loop and none lands. Cover any two layers: the remaining one should still hint at the same idea.

## Variants and the hook check

1. Write 5 variants from at least three of the seven patterns in `references/hook-patterns.md` (borrowed authority + giveaway, name the viewer then a number, one object one number one twist, price shock, pain, verdict or conflict, own authority).
2. Score each with one point per yes:
   1. Does the spoken line open a gap (a question or tension the viewer needs closed) within about 10 words?
   2. Does it say who it's for, or what is at stake?
   3. Does it carry one concrete number, object or twist instead of a vague claim?
   4. Does it leave the answer for later?
   5. Does frame 0 plus the title work with the sound off?
   6. Is every claim true to the facts sheet?
3. Pick the variant with the most points. Drop any variant that fails question 6.

## The frame-0 title (`episode.json` "hook")

Every reel opens on its hook. The `hook` key in `episode.json` puts the cover title on screen from frame 0 (`build_vo.py` writes it into `plan.json`) and holds the banner back until the title leaves.

```
"hook": {"lines": [["AI", "LEAKED"], ["13,000+"]], "hot": ["13,000+"], "until": "yes", "size": 108, "top": 220}
```

- `lines`: the WRITE text as torn tags, one array of words per line. `hot`: the words that get the yellow tag.
- The title leaves at the onset of the `until` word (`["yes", 2]` for its 2nd occurrence), or after `"hold"` seconds (default 2.4).
- Title stays 2-5 words and shares no words with SAY.

## The cut out of the hook carries motion

A hook that ends on a held pose feels abrupt and drops the attention it just earned.
- Give the hook scene's last ~10 frames an accelerating push (a tiny pull back first).
- Scene 2 opens on an impact at its focal prop, then the camera eases back to the set. For example, the proof card slams onto the board with a `stamp`, the camera starts at 1.17x, and a character scurries in from off-frame.
- End the title on the cut with `"hook": {"hold": <S01 seconds>}` so it lifts away during the push instead of covering scene 2's first frames.

## Gate

- [ ] SHOW is mid-action on frame 0 and reads muted.
- [ ] WRITE is on frame 0 and isn't the spoken words.
- [ ] SAY opens the gap within 10 words.
- [ ] All three pass the alignment test, and ALIGN names the one idea.
- [ ] The winning variant scored best and passed question 6.

## Hand-off

Write the HOOK block at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/papercut/STORYBOARD.md` (create the file if it isn't there). Note the hook's key word or number; the script's last line repeats it. Next is `papercut-script`, which also puts SAY into line `l1_hook` of `narration/script.json`.

## 1. Render stills

From the project's `papercut/` folder:

```
$PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/qa.sh NAME FROM-TO NTH [SCALE=0.3] [COLS=9]
```

- Use 4-6 timestamps per check. For a scene, NTH is about its length in frames divided by 4. Leave `FROM-TO` out for the whole reel and raise NTH.
- The output is `out/qa/NAME_0.jpg` (and `_1`, `_2` for longer ranges), at most 45 frames per sheet. Read the sheet; keep sheets small.
- One QA command per scene, and never two renders at once. Keep fixes to two rounds per scene.
- Check against the storyboard: the scene's frame 0, its key events on their words, nothing clipped, nothing covering the banner or caption bands.

## 2. Checklist

- [ ] Every object reads as paper: grain, rough edge, drop shadow, stacked-piece shading, no outlines or gradients.
- [ ] The world camera moves smoothly. Only the banner and labels boil (stepped, subtle).
- [ ] The banner is fixed in position and taped, 3-7 words, one fact each, never repeats the VO. The banners alone read as a fact sheet.
- [ ] Every set illustrates a concrete word in its VO line, numbers are physical props, and there is one callback set before the CTA.
- [ ] Every number and UI label traces to the facts list. The script has at least one honest limitation and a feature stack of exactly three.
- [ ] Captions: one tag per word, tilted, popping on onset, pages of 1-3, in the 68-80% band, never on a face.
- [ ] Saturation only on characters, captions and signals.
- [ ] A visual event on every stressed word, with ambient motion always running.
- [ ] Cuts on banner changes (sets 1.5-3 s in tours and news, up to 5 s in a metaphor beat), bottom 20% clear.
- [ ] **The HOOK block (SAY / WRITE / SHOW / ALIGN) is on screen exactly as written:** frame 0 shows the SHOW moment mid-action with the WRITE title on it, and the first VO line is SAY.
- [ ] Every scene has a camera move, at most one page turn or tear, a tape pull or whip into the CTA, and every transition has its SFX.
- [ ] Humour pass visible on screen: one format throughout, a costume prop per idea, one struggling beat, the frame-0 prop returns changed in the CTA set, and every gag reads in under 1 s and never covers the banner, the captions or the key number.
- [ ] Vocabulary in the VO and banners matches the audience level in `SERIES.md`.
- [ ] Voiceover, captions and events are in sync (scrub the Studio at every cut).

For a failed item, fix the scene file (or the kit in the library, never `src/lib/` in the project) and re-run the one scene. Rebuild a scene with `papercut-build`.

Open the Studio preview, list the scenes with timings, and say what is placeholder: voice, music, SFX, assets. If the voice is a placeholder, say how to re-voice it (`papercut-voice`). After posting, the numbers go to `papercut-strategy` for the autopsy.

Fixes go back to `papercut-build` (scene or sound) or `papercut-voice` (sync). A clean pass ends the reel: render with `$PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/render.sh` when the user asks.

# Papercut script

Research, script, banner track, staging and gags are written together, because each one feeds the others. The full system, with the phrase bank and two staged examples, is `references/storytelling.md`. Gag and format banks: `references/comedy.md`.

Every beat runs three tracks that do different jobs:
- **Voiceover** (shown as caption tags): tells the story, casual and second person, changes every sentence.
- **Banner**: adds the hard fact, number or honest caveat the voiceover skips, changes every 1.8-3 s.
- **Set**: literally illustrates a concrete noun from the voiceover, with the product UI doing the demo, changes with the banner.

## Preflight

- Install: Minimal is enough. Resolve `$PAPERCUT_LIB` only if you want the backdrop sheet (`library/papercut/public/bg/backdrops/_sheet.jpg`) when choosing sets. Each image costs about 0.7-1.5k tokens, so open only what the step needs.
- Needs the BRIEF at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/research/facts.md` and the HOOK block at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/papercut/STORYBOARD.md`. Missing one: run `papercut-strategy` or `papercut-hook` first.
- Research needs web fetch or search, and any browser tool for screenshots. Without them, ask the user for screenshots and facts.

## 1. Research and rough UI

- Collect facts from the source with a source for each: name, maker, numbers, price, requirements, limitations, competitor numbers. Mark anything uncertain.
- Grab the key screens (2-4), real labels and button text, the accent colour and hero images. The video rebuilds a rough version of the UI as papercut props, not a screen recording (`references/storytelling.md` section 5).
- Confirm the role framing from the BRIEF. Never invent product behaviour. See the role-framing note in `../papercut-explainer/references/frame-breakdown.md`.
- Write the list to `research/facts.md` under the BRIEF. Every number in the script, banners and UI must trace back to it.

## 2. Pick the mode

| Mode | When |
|---|---|
| Open-source drop | A free or local alternative to a paid product |
| News launch / worth-it | A new paid tier, model or feature from a big company |
| Feature unlock / how-to | A hidden setting or command that changes how a tool works |

Hook formulas and the middle of each mode: `references/storytelling.md` section 6. Apply the hook update: open the gap and the stake, not the news.

## 3. Script on the spine

Write 75-95 words for 22-30 s, about 3.5-4 words a second, inside the chosen format, with a new set every 1.5-3 s. The 10 beats:

1. Hook (0-3 s), already fixed by `papercut-hook`
2. Proof or tension
3. Reframe ("So instead of..., you can...")
4. Name reveal ("It's called...", never before the hook)
5. How it works, one concrete demo
6. Escalation ("And X is just the start, because..." plus a stack of exactly three)
7. Peak ("And get this:" plus the biggest number)
8. Catch (the honest counterpoint)
9. Payoff ("which means...")
10. CTA ("Good thing I made [freebie]. For the link, comment KEYWORD.")

Shorten beats rather than speeding up the voice. Rules:
- Second person, contractions, short clauses joined by "and", "because", "which means". Vocabulary at the audience level in `SERIES.md`.
- Name a big brand in the first sentence, even when the subject is something else.
- Every number is concrete and sourced. One feature stack, always three items.
- At least one real limitation, in the VO or the banners. The CTA keyword is one short word tied to the topic.
- The last line repeats the hook's key word or number, then gives the keyword.

Write it to `narration/script.json` as `[{"id": "l1_hook", "text": "..."}, ...]`, one line per sentence or clause group. Line `l1_hook` is SAY from the HOOK block. Mark the one or two words each line leans on (the number, the twist word, the verdict) in the staging table; `papercut-voice` uses them.

## 4. Banner track

10-18 banners, 3-7 words, ALL CAPS, one fact each, about one every 2-3 s. They never repeat the VO: read alone they are a fact sheet. Include a headline stat, a price translation, a credibility fact, availability, at least one honest caveat, at least one trust or safety fact, feature claims, at least one competitor contrast, and a range/decision banner before the CTA. Types and examples: `references/storytelling.md` section 3.

## 5. Staging table

One row per banner, written into `STORYBOARD.md` under the HOOK block:

`t (s)` | VO words under it | BANNER | SET (room + bg colour) | HERO PROP (a visual pun from the VO's concrete noun) | PRODUCT UI moment | MASCOT action and costume prop | GAG

- A new set for every banner, background colours rotating. The set illustrates a word in the VO line, not the banner.
- Numbers become physical props: price signs, scales, multiplier walls, gauges, meters, races. Competitors appear as pinned cards, never as the hero.
- The mascot is the viewer's proxy and reacts. Product UI is a rough rebuild on a paper monitor or laptop with fake interactions.
- One callback to an earlier set before the CTA. The CTA set shows a comment box typing the keyword.
- `papercut-storyboard` adds the camera and transition columns.

## 6. Humour pass (after the script, before staging is final)

Add the GAG column. The voiceover stays straight; only the picture is silly.
1. One format for the whole reel.
2. One gag per banner that acts out the point, from `references/comedy.md`.
3. A costume prop per idea. The mascot's own item stays on and gets one prop on top.
4. One struggling-mascot beat, on the catch line.
5. A prop on frame 0 that returns changed in the CTA set (I'M OUT becomes FREE).
6. One absurd, unexplained background moment.
7. At most one meme, rebuilt in the series' own style, never a real clip, still or audio.

No gag may cover the banner, the captions or the key number, and each must read in under 1 s.

## Gate

- [ ] 75-95 words, 22-30 s, one honest limitation, a stack of exactly three.
- [ ] Every number and banner traces to `facts.md`; banners alone read as a fact sheet.
- [ ] Last line repeats the hook's key word or number.
- [ ] Humour pass done: costume per idea, a struggling beat, a returning prop, one absurd moment, at most one meme.

## Hand-off

Next is `papercut-storyboard`. It reads `narration/script.json` and the HOOK block and staging table in `episodes/NN-slug/papercut/STORYBOARD.md`. For a script-only run, stop here and give the user those files. The copy-paste storytelling prompt for another tool is `references/storytelling.md` section 7.

# Papercut setup

A guided wrapper around `install.sh`. It checks what is installed, asks how much the user wants, runs the installer non-interactively and reports. Use it whenever another papercut skill finds something missing.

## Preflight

- Find the repo root (where `install.sh` lives): `readlink` on the installed skill folder ends in `<root>/skills/papercut-setup`. Look in each harness's skills folder in turn (the table is `harnesses.sh`; typically `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.config/opencode/skills`, or the same under `<project>/`). Failing that, `PAPERCUT_HOME=` in `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/papercut-explainer/config.env`. If neither exists, the skills probably came from `npx skills add` (skills only, no library). Ask where to clone the repo (default `~/papercut-explainer`), run `git clone https://github.com/0xS4N4TG/papercut-explainer <dir>`, and use that as the root. The installer then replaces the copied skill folders with links into the checkout (it backs up real folders first). Never guess a path.
- Run every `install.sh` command from that root. It needs bash, and macOS or Linux (Windows: use WSL).
- The installer's own prompts need a terminal, which the agent's shell tool lacks. Always pass `--yes` and the answers as flags. Tell the user they can run `./install.sh` themselves for the interactive menu.

## 1. Doctor

```
./install.sh --doctor
```

Add `--project DIR`, `--skills-dir DIR` or `--target <names>` if the skills went somewhere other than the detected defaults; the doctor only looks where you point it, and with no `--target` one complete install location is enough. It prints `[ok]`, `[--]` (missing) or `[!!]` (wrong). Summarise it in plain words:
- skills installed, config file and `PAPERCUT_LIB`
- node 20+, npm, ffmpeg, python3
- Remotion agent skills, Python tools (numpy + Pillow)
- voice: `qwen_tts` importable, a CustomVoice model in the Hugging Face cache
- library files present

Then say which install mode that adds up to (see `papercut-explainer`, Install modes).

## 2. Ask

Ask only what is still open, in one call (your agent's question tool, for example AskUserQuestion in Claude Code). Run `./install.sh --dry-run --mode minimal --yes` first if you need to know which harnesses it detected (`--target auto`, the default):

| Question | Options |
|---|---|
| How much? | **Minimal**: skills only, seconds. **Standard**: render with a placeholder voice, ~0.7 GB and a few minutes. **Full**: Standard + local voiceover, +4-6 GB (a 1.5 GB venv plus a 2.3 or 4.2 GB model) and a 2-minute smoke test. **Custom**: pick components. |
| Which agents? | **Detected on this machine** (default, `--target auto`; Claude Code if none), a list such as `--target claude,codex,gemini`, or `--target all`. Names are in `harnesses.sh`; the README's *Works with* table says which are tested. |
| Where do the skills go? | User-wide (the default) or one project (`--project DIR`). |
| Copy or link? | Symlink (default, updates with `git pull`) or `--copy` (a snapshot). |
| Scene-agent model, per agent with file subagents (`claude`, `opencode`, `codex`, `gemini`; skip the rest)? | One question per selected agent, each with **Inherit** (use the session model) as an option. Claude Code: **Sonnet** (default: cheapest, what the scene agents were tuned on) · **Opus** (strongest; every parallel scene agent bills at Opus rates) · **Haiku** · Inherit. Maps to `--claude-model sonnet\|opus\|haiku\|inherit\|<id>`. Other agents: default **Inherit**, or a model id in that agent's own format (opencode `provider/model-id`, for example `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`; Codex and Gemini plain ids). Maps to `--opencode-model M` or `--agent-model codex=M`. |
| Another provider's model (DeepSeek and others)? | Only if the user asks. Connect the provider inside the agent first (OpenCode `/connect`; Codex `config.toml` provider; Claude Code's `ANTHROPIC_*` variables), then pass its model id as above. The README's *Models other than Claude* section has the steps and the DeepSeek ids. Say plainly that it is untested end to end and that weaker models cost more QA rounds. |
| TTS model size (Full) | 1.7B, better prosody, ~4.2 GB (default). 0.6B, lighter and faster, ~2.3 GB. |
| Voice-clone model (Full) | No (default), or `--with-clone`: the Base model of the same size again. |

Confirm before any multi-GB download. On a machine with no GPU (not Apple Silicon, no NVIDIA), TTS generation takes minutes per line; suggest recording the voiceover or the placeholder voice instead.

## 3. Install

```
./install.sh --mode <minimal|standard|full> --yes [--target auto|all|claude,codex,...] [--claude-model M] [--opencode-model M] [--agent-model NAME=M] [--skills-dir DIR | --project DIR] [--copy] [--tts-model 1.7B|0.6B] [--with-clone]
./install.sh --mode custom --components skills,deps,remotion-skills,pytools,tts,verify --yes
```

- Add `--dry-run` first if the user wants to see the plan; it changes nothing.
- The scene-builder agent is written as a **copy** per harness, in that harness's own format (Claude and OpenCode markdown, Codex TOML, Gemini markdown), with the chosen model line or none for Inherit. To change a model later: `./install.sh --mode custom --components skills --target codex --agent-model codex=<id> --yes` (or `--claude-model`, `--opencode-model`).
- Standard and Full take minutes (npm install, Remotion's Chrome, venvs, model download). Run them in the background and check the output; do not hold a foreground call.
- What each mode does: Minimal links the skills and the scene-builder agent (into each selected harness's skills and agents folders). Standard adds a dependency check, the Remotion agent skills (`npx skills add remotion-dev/skills -g -y -a <harness id>` once per selected harness, installed user-wide, so say so when you confirm the plan), a Python venv with numpy, Pillow and soundfile, and a self-test render. - The installer writes `PAPERCUT_HOME`, `PAPERCUT_LIB`, `PAPERCUT_PY`, `QWEN_TTS_PY` and `ASR_PY` into `~/.config/papercut-explainer/config.env`. An existing skill folder that differs from this checkout is backed up to `~/.config/papercut-explainer/backups/` (not into the skills folder, so it is not loaded twice); an identical copy, such as one from `npx skills add`, is just replaced.

## 4. Verify and report

Run `./install.sh --doctor` again with the same `--project`, `--skills-dir` or `--target`. Report what is installed, which scene-agent model each agent got, what failed (the installer prints `needs attention:` with component names), and the fix. A new Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI session picks up newly linked skills (restart it); opencode reloads configuration automatically. Then suggest: "make a papercut explainer about <link>", or one stage at a time ("write a hook for...", "storyboard this script", "set up the voice").

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `node` older than 20, or missing | Install Node 20+ (nodejs.org, `brew install node`), then `./install.sh --mode custom --components deps,verify --yes`. |
| `ffmpeg` missing | `brew install ffmpeg` or `apt install ffmpeg`. |
| Voice venv: "need Python 3.10-3.12" | Qwen3-TTS has no wheels for newer Python. Install `uv` (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) or `brew install python@3.12`, rerun the `tts` component. |
| Hugging Face download stalls or fails | Rerun; finished files are kept and the script retries 3 times. It sets `HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1`; set it yourself for manual downloads. |
| First render is slow | Remotion downloads its headless Chrome once. The audio render and `capture.mjs` use your own Chrome; set `CHROME_PATH` if it isn't in a usual place. |
| Self-test fails | Run `library/tools/selftest.sh` directly to see the failing step. |
| Skills don't show | Restart Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI (opencode reloads). Check the harness's folder (`harnesses.sh`; `~/.agents/skills` for most) and run `./install.sh --doctor`. |
| opencode: "Configuration is invalid ... tools" | An old copy of the Claude agent file sits in an opencode agents folder. Rerun `./install.sh --target opencode`; it writes the opencode version. |
| Scene agents cost too much, or run on the wrong model | Rerun the skills step with another model: `./install.sh --mode custom --components skills --claude-model sonnet --yes` (or `--opencode-model inherit`). `inherit` means the session model. |
| Move from Minimal to Standard | `./install.sh --mode custom --components deps,remotion-skills,pytools,verify --yes` |
| Add the voice later | `./install.sh --mode custom --components tts --yes [--tts-model 0.6B] [--with-clone]` |
| Remove it | `./install.sh --uninstall` removes the links it recorded. It leaves `config.env`, the venvs under `~/.local/share/papercut-explainer` and the Hugging Face cache; delete those by hand for the space. |
| Windows | Not supported directly. Use WSL. |

# Papercut storyboard

The storyboard is the plan every scene is built from. It names the camera move and the cut for every scene, so the scene agent doesn't invent them. A brief that says "CameraPush or your own transform" gets a flat push or a hand-rolled zoom in every scene, and the kit's camera moves go unused.

## Preflight

- Install: Minimal is enough. With a library, check `library/papercut/CATALOG.md` (sections "paper/camera.tsx" and "paper/transitions.tsx") for each move's props and when it fits. If the file is missing or stale, run `python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/catalog.py`. Resolve `$PAPERCUT_LIB` from the environment, else the `PAPERCUT_LIB=` line in `~/.config/papercut-explainer/config.env`, else ask once.
- Needs `narration/script.json` and `papercut/STORYBOARD.md` with the HOOK block and the staging table (banner, set, prop, UI moment, mascot, gag per row). Missing: run `papercut-hook` and `papercut-script`.
- Backdrop sheet for choosing sets: `library/papercut/public/bg/backdrops/_sheet.jpg`. Open only what the step needs.

## 1. Global rules

Put these at the top of `STORYBOARD.md`, under the HOOK block. Palette by role (rotate background colours per set): `../papercut-explainer/references/style-guide.md` section 5. Fonts: section 6. Canvas and zones: section 4. A feature-unlock that suits one extended metaphor can use section 12.
- 1080x1920, 30 fps. Banner at 14-21% height, caption band 68-80% (it shifts per scene to stay off faces), bottom 20% clear.
- Light from the top-left. Saturation only on characters, captions and signals.

## 2. Camera / Cut table

One row per scene, before the scene blocks. Every row names a component from the kit's `paper/camera.tsx` and the `CutSeries` kind (from `paper/transitions.tsx`) for the cut into that scene.

| Scene | Camera (`paper/camera.tsx`) | Cut in (`CutSeries` kind) |
|---|---|---|
| S01Hook | `OrbitCamera` + `Depth`, `SnapZoom` on "<word>" | none |
| S04Name | `Crane` rise to <focal prop> | `tearAway` |
| S09Peak | `CrabTrack` along <lineup> | `whip` |
| S10CTA | `RackFocus` <prop> to phone | `tapePull` |

- Camera options: `OrbitCamera` + `Depth`, `SnapZoom`, `Crane`, `CrabTrack`, `DollyZoom`, `RackFocus`, `ForegroundPass`, `DutchTilt`, `FocusPulse`, `FreezeFrame`, `PullBack`, `PovMask`, `TimeRamp`, `TiltShift`, `FocusHunt`, `Handheld`, and `CameraPush` (from `paper/kit.tsx`). The catalog's `paper/camera.tsx` section says when each fits.
- Cut options: `hard`, `whip`, `zoomThrough`, `pageTurn`, `tearAway`, `tapePull`, `stampCut`, `infiniteZoom`, `popUpBook`, `keyhole`, `burnAway`.
- A plain `CameraPush` is allowed on at most a third of the scenes.
- Copy each row's camera into its scene block header. The cut column goes into `episode.json` as `"cuts": {"S04Name": {"kind": "tearAway"}}` (no entry means a hard cut), which `papercut-build` fills.

## 3. Scene blocks

One block per scene, 1.5-5 s each, cutting on sentence boundaries:

```
## S03: <beat>  (5.6-8.2 s, 78 f)   BANNER: <TAKEAWAY IN CAPS>
Location/bg: <world location + bg colour>     Camera: <camera.tsx component + params, from the table>   Cut in: <kind>
Cast: <who, accessories>                       Caption band: y=0.76
| VO word (stressed) | frame | event                                    | motion spec                   |
| "<word>"           | +6    | <prop enters / state flips / acts>       | <spring/slide/swap + frames>  |
Ambient: <LED blink, idle bob, stars, screen waveform>
Boil: banner + labels, +-1.5 px every 2 frames
SFX: <pop, chime, click...>
```

- Expand each staging-table row into frame-level events: one per stressed word (every 0.4-0.8 s), ambient motion always on. Frames are offsets from the word, later read with `cueOf(ID)(word, n)`.
- Product UI is the rough rebuild on a paper monitor or laptop, with fake interactions (cursor click, typing, progress, waveform, list scroll).
- **Proof:** once per reel, a real screenshot of the source page (a browser capture via `library/tools/capture.mjs`, not a redraw) taped onto a paper card, with a red marker circle drawing itself around the key line. Everything else stays a rough papercut rebuild.
- One callback to an earlier set before the CTA.

## 4. Camera and transition rules

- Every scene has one move. A slow push is the baseline. Add a parallax orbit on lit sets for depth, a punch-in or snap zoom on the stressed word for numbers and jokes, a foreground pass (blurred paper object across the lens) or rack focus, a pull-back to reveal scale, and a freeze frame with a label on the struggling-mascot beat.
- Mostly hard cuts on the banner change. A whip-pan with motion blur on 2-3 topic changes, a zoom-through when going "inside" a screen, door or mirror, at most one page turn or tear per reel (on the catch or a before/after contrast), and the tape pull into the CTA (a plain kraft strip, with an optional `label` to print a word on it).
- The cut out of the hook carries motion through it. Apply the rule from `papercut-hook` to S01 and S02.
- Transitions run 6-12 frames, each with its SFX (whip, zoom, page-flip, rip, tape-peel).
- In a library project, chain scenes with the kit's transition series, which keeps every scene start on its `plan.json` frame so the voice stays in sync.

## 5. SFX plan

- Air sounds (whoosh, slide, whip, zoom) together: at most one every 2.5 s of reel. `cues.py` prints a note above that. For scale, 12 in 33 s is fine and 24 in 26 s is distracting.
- Entrances get contact sounds (pop, thud, stamp) or silence. Count them in `tools/cues.json` before the audio render.
- Name SFX from `library/audio/CATALOG.md` in each block's `SFX:` line. Scene agents write the real rows to `tools/cue_sheet.d/<Scene>.json`.
- Pick the bed preset (`episode.json` "bed") and set `cutSfx` to match the cut kinds: `tearAway` rip, `tapePull` tape-peel.

## Gate

- [ ] Every scene has a camera and a cut-in, and a plain `CameraPush` is on at most a third of them.
- [ ] Every stressed word has an event; ambient motion is listed.
- [ ] One proof beat, one callback, the tape pull or whip into the CTA.
- [ ] At most one page turn or tear; air sounds within budget.

- Name the anticipation and the one exaggerated beat in each scene block's event table. The 12 principles, mapped to kit components, are in `../papercut-explainer/references/motion-principles.md`.

## Hand-off

Next is `papercut-build`, which scaffolds the project and turns the Camera / Cut table and scene boundaries into `episode.json`. It reads `STORYBOARD.md` and `narration/script.json`. The Timing section of `STORYBOARD.md` is generated later, after the voice, so leave it out.

# Papercut strategy

These notes decide what a reel says and why it holds attention. The other papercut skills decide how it is written, staged and built. The rules come from studying high-performing faceless tech reels and from reading platform insights after posting. Keep your own evidence in the series' `research/analytics/`.

## Preflight

- Install: Minimal is enough. No library needed.
- Find the series folder and read its `SERIES.md` first. It holds the audience (who, level, regions to aim for and avoid), voice, palette and mascot notes, the visual style, the keyword log and what has worked so far. If it is missing, ask the user for those fields and write the file.
- For a competitor study: `yt-dlp`, `ffmpeg` and any speech-to-text tool. For an autopsy: the platform's insights numbers from the user.

## 1. Topic

- Re-skin proven winners. A topic that worked (for you or a competitor) in a new familiar format beats a new topic in a plain format. Example: a reel about running several AI agents as a council, remade as "a jury of 12 AIs puts your idea on trial".
- The viewer must be able to use the outcome. If they can't do anything with it, skip it.
- Something to give away: every winner promises a free skill, prompt, template, cheat sheet or setup by DM.
- Speed on a hot repo. The first reel on a trending repo takes most of the views. Ship within a day or two, on an angle the earlier reels didn't use (`../papercut-hook/references/hook-patterns.md`).
- Demand signals: competitor outliers (likes at 5x or more of their median), trending repos (stars per day), front-page threads, same-day launches. Save candidates to the series' idea backlog.

## 2. Format

Pick one familiar real-world format for the whole reel before writing a word: courtroom, pitch show, cooking show, heist movie, nature documentary, dating show, character-select screen, boss fight, job interview, Olympic podium. The viewer gets the premise in a second and every set and gag comes from it. A plain list of facts has no premise to grasp, so it gets less attention than the same facts told inside a format. The bank, with the story each format carries, is `../papercut-script/references/comedy.md`.

## 3. Audience level

Write at the level `SERIES.md` sets. There is no default audience. The feeling to leave behind: you're not behind, and now you know something most people don't.

## 4. Funnel and caption

- Spoken CTA: "Good thing I made [freebie]. For the link, comment KEYWORD." One short keyword tied to the topic.
- Deliver the freebie by DM with whatever comment-to-DM tooling the account allows. Keep sends slow and spaced, because platforms rate-limit bursts.
- Caption: the hook as the first line, a follow line so the DM lands, "READ BELOW" with the useful part written out, one send prompt ("Send this to the friend who..."), 3-5 hashtags.
- Shares matter most to the algorithm. A funny or useful reel gets sent.

## 5. Write the BRIEF

Put this block at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/research/facts.md`. `papercut-hook` and `papercut-script` read it.

```
BRIEF
Source:   <link(s)>
Claim:    <the one claim the video proves>
Role:     <who or what does the work vs who advises or approves>
Mode:     open-source drop | news launch / worth-it | feature unlock
Format:   <the one familiar format>
Audience: <level, copied from SERIES.md>
CTA:      <KEYWORD> -> <the freebie>
Length:   22-30 s
```

## 6. Competitor study (when the user shares reels)

Method, setup and the subagent prompt: `references/competitor-analysis.md`.
- One subagent per reel, up to 4 at a time. Each downloads the reel, extracts frames at 2 fps, transcribes it, applies the six-question hook check and returns a fixed-format report.
- Synthesise into a comparison table (likes and comments vs the creator's typical reel, age at fetch, look, length), what drove the outliers, what to borrow and what stays your difference.
- Save it to `research/analytics/YYYY-MM-DD-<creator>-reels.md`. One reel is noise; look for a pattern across 4 or more.

## 7. After posting: the autopsy

- At about 2 h and 24 h collect views, skip rate, average watch time, the retention curve, likes, comments, saves, shares, follows, traffic source, top countries and ages.
- Read them in this order: hook, topic, format, audience, timing. Fix the earliest thing that failed before touching later ones.
- If most viewers are gone by 3-5 s, or the skip rate is clearly worse than your own median, the hook failed. Run `papercut-hook`.
- Write `research/analytics/YYYY-MM-DD-autopsy.md` and update `SERIES.md` with what changed.

## Gate

- [ ] `SERIES.md` read; audience, regions and voice respected.
- [ ] Topic has a demand signal, a usable outcome and a freebie by DM.
- [ ] One format named in a line.
- [ ] Vocabulary and the DM match the audience level.
- [ ] BRIEF written; caption planned.

## Hand-off

Next is `papercut-hook`. It reads the BRIEF in `episodes/NN-slug/research/facts.md` and writes the HOOK block at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/papercut/STORYBOARD.md`. If the episode folder isn't scaffolded yet, create `research/` and `papercut/` by hand; `papercut-build` merges them when it scaffolds.

# Papercut voice

Every later stage needs two things in the narration folder: `voice/final_narrator/<id>.wav` (one WAV per script line) and `timing_narrator.js` (a start and end for every word). This skill produces them by one of three paths, then builds the captions and the scene plan. The full reference for the scripts is `library/voice/README.md`.

## Preflight

- Library: `$PAPERCUT_LIB`, else the `PAPERCUT_LIB=` line in `~/.config/papercut-explainer/config.env`, else ask once. Export it, and `. "$PAPERCUT_LIB/env.sh"` loads `ASR_PY`, `QWEN_TTS_PY` and the other config values into the shell.
- A scaffolded project (`papercut-build`, step 1) with `narration/script.json` and `papercut/episode.json` holding `scenes`. `new_episode.sh` copies `build_timing.py` into `narration/`.
- If the user already has a TTS installed, use it as it is and don't rebuild it (path B, or A if it is Qwen3-TTS). Ask once which one and where it runs. Otherwise ask which path, and say what it needs:

| Path | Needs | Install mode |
|---|---|---|
| A. Local Qwen3-TTS | the voice venv from `library/voice/setup_tts.sh` (model download 2.3-4.2 GB) | Full |
| B. Your own recording or another TTS | an ASR backend (mlx-whisper or faster-whisper) and librosa + numpy for the pitch pass, in the Python that `ASR_PY` and `QWEN_TTS_PY` name | Full, or those packages by hand |
| C. Placeholder | ffmpeg; macOS for `--say` | Standard |

If the path needs more than the install has, run `./install.sh --doctor` and hand over to `papercut-setup`. Without ASR, `build_timing.py` only estimates 2.75 words a second, so captions drift against real audio.

## Path A: local Qwen3-TTS

From the series folder:

```
cp $PAPERCUT_LIB/voice/voice.example.json voice/voice.json     # once per series; edit it
$PAPERCUT_LIB/voice/narrate.sh voice/voice.json episodes/NN-slug/narration
$PAPERCUT_LIB/voice/finalize.sh voice/voice.json episodes/NN-slug/narration episodes/NN-slug/narration/voice/takes/narrator [num.json]
```

- `voice.json`: `speaker` (CustomVoice: Aiden, Dylan, Eric, Ryan, Serena, Vivian, Sohee, Ono_anna, Uncle_fu) and `instruct`. Recommended: CustomVoice 1.7B, Ryan or Aiden, instruct *"friendly, natural, conversational, like telling a friend; clear pauses between sentences; stress the key word of each line"*. `takes_per_line` defaults to 3. `tempo` stays 1.0 (other values need `rubberband`). `qa_targets` set the pitch range and the ASR match (0.9).
- A script line can carry `tts` (respelled text for pronunciation; captions keep `text`) and its own `instruct`. `num.json` maps numerals to spoken words (`{"13,000": "thirteen thousand"}`) so ASR matching doesn't fail on digits.
- Run one TTS process at a time; the 1.7B model is memory-hungry.
- `finalize.sh` runs ASR and pitch on every take, picks one per line, trims, loudness-normalises to -16 LUFS, re-runs ASR on the finals and writes `timing_narrator.js`. After listening, put corrections in `voice/picks_override.json` (`{"l3_name": 2}`) and rerun with `SKIP_PICK=1`.
- Voice Design (describing a voice in words) is a Qwen3-TTS mode that `narrate.py` doesn't drive. Generate with it elsewhere and use path B.

## Path B: your own recording or another TTS

- Put one WAV per line in `voice/final_narrator/<id>.wav`, or raw takes as `voice/takes/narrator/<id>_<k>.wav` and run `finalize.sh` as above.
- For finished lines, transcribe them, write `voice/chosen_narrator.json` as `{id: "voice/final_narrator/<id>.wav"}`, then from `narration/`:

```
$ASR_PY $PAPERCUT_LIB/voice/asr.py voice/final_narrator/*.wav > voice/asr_narrator_final.json
CHOSEN=voice/chosen_narrator.json TIMING_OUT=timing_narrator.js python3 build_timing.py voice/asr_narrator_final.json
```

## Path C: placeholder

From the `narration/` folder:

```
python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/placeholder_vo.py [--wps 3.0] [--say [VOICE]]
```

It writes silent WAVs (or the macOS `say` voice with `--say`) and `timing_narrator.js` from `script.json` alone, spreading word times by word length. `--wps 3.5` to `4` approximates the target pace (default 3.0). The reel can be built and timed first and re-voiced later: swap the WAVs, rerun `finalize.sh`, rerun `build_vo.py`, and the word cues follow.

## Delivery rules

Delivery is human, unhurried and emphasised. The viewer must follow every line on the first listen.
- **Breathing room.** A real pause at every sentence end and between list beats ("Fine. Fine. Fine."). Start with 0.3-0.4 s between lines (`gap` in `episode.json`, default 0.22; `gaps` adds an extra beat after one named line) and judge by ear. Pauses go at sentence or clause boundaries only: a 0.2 s gap inside a phrase, such as "copied it, | by taking...", reads as lag. Use the 30 s ceiling for air instead of cutting pauses, and never slow the tempo to get it.
- **Emphasis.** The one or two words each line leans on (the number, the twist word, the verdict) come from the script's staging table. Pass them as a per-line `instruct`.
- **Tone.** Conversational and a little amused, not announcer energy. Questions sound like real questions, the catch line sounds curious, the CTA is warm. The narrator still doesn't joke; the picture does.
- **Clone model (no instructions).** With a clone voice (`ref_audio` + `ref_text`, Base model) the levers are the text and the take. Write the pauses into the punctuation (full stops between list beats, a short question as its own sentence). Generate several seeds of one continuous take (`SEED_BASE`, `takes_per_line`), pick the one with the most pitch movement on the target words and ASR 0.9 or better, and re-take a flat line alone (`ONLY=l4_peak`) and splice it at a sentence boundary. Only clone a voice you have the right to use.
- **Whole script at once** gives consistent prosody: generate one take, `split_take.py` cuts it per line, then set `"gap": 0` in `episode.json`. Per scene is fine if the user prefers.
- **Play the first three lines to the user before the full run**: `ONLY=l1_hook,l2_...,l3_... narrate.sh ...`.

## Captions and timing

From `papercut/`, once `episode.json` has `scenes`:

```
python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/build_vo.py     # public/vo/voiceover.wav, public/vo/captions.json, src/plan.json
python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/timing_md.py    # Timing section of STORYBOARD.md
```

`captions.json` is a Remotion `Caption[]`; scene boundaries come from the word timestamps; the composition length is `plan.json`'s `durationInFrames`. `build_vo.py` flags any scene under 1.2 s. With no library, transcribe the WAV with the Remotion captions skill (whisper.cpp) or any speech-to-text tool that returns word timestamps.

Captions are one torn tag per word, pages of 1-3 words, at 3.5-4 words a second (`../papercut-explainer/references/style-guide.md`, sections 11 and 13).

## Hand-off

Next is `papercut-build` (stubs, scenes, sound, render). It reads `src/plan.json` and the Timing section of `papercut/STORYBOARD.md`. Any later voice change reruns `build_vo.py` and `timing_md.py`; the scene cache then re-renders everything.

# papercut-explainer

Make short vertical explainer reels that look like layered construction paper, with the coding agent you already use doing the work: Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot and any other tool that reads Agent Skills.

![A two-scene reel built with the library: hook title, parallax camera, word-by-word captions, a tape-pull cut and a comment-keyword CTA](docs/img/hello-reel.gif)

*The bundled example reel ([`examples/hello-reel`](examples/hello-reel)), rendered from this repo. Silent placeholder voice, real captions, camera and cuts.*

This repo is two things that work together:

- **Nine agent skills** (the open `SKILL.md` format, so they load in most coding agents; see [Works with](#works-with)) that run the whole pipeline: strategy, hook, script, storyboard, voice, build, QA, and an installer. Ask for a reel, or run one stage on its own.
- **A Remotion library** the skills build on: a paper-cut component kit, 24 backdrops, 17 camera moves, 10 scene transitions, film-look layers, 79 sound effects and 8 music beds, plus the scripts that tie them into an episode.

You describe the video ("explain this repo in 25 seconds"). The skills research it, write a script on a fixed spoken spine, plan every camera move and cut, make or fake the voiceover, and build the scenes in Remotion. You review stills and the final cut.

## Contents

[What is in the box](#what-is-in-the-box) · [Install](#install) · [Use it](#use-it) · [Examples](#examples) · [How the workflow runs](#how-the-workflow-runs) · [Voice](#voice) · [Customising](#customising) · [Requirements](#requirements) · [Cost](#cost) · [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) · [Limits](#limits) · [Licence](#licence)

|---|---|

## Install

You need Node 20+, npm, ffmpeg, rsync and Python 3. Any coding agent in [Works with](#works-with) is the front end.

**With `npx skills`** (skills only, fastest):

```bash
npx skills add 0xS4N4TG/papercut-explainer
```

This installs the nine skills into your agents' skill folders (the CLI supports about 80 agents). It does not fetch the Remotion library or the scripts. Open your agent and say "set up papercut-explainer": `papercut-setup` clones the repo, asks how much you want (Minimal, Standard, Full) and installs it. Add `-g` for a user-wide install, `--skill papercut-hook` to take one skill.

**With git** (everything, including the library):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/0xS4N4TG/papercut-explainer
cd papercut-explainer
./install.sh
```

By default the installer looks for coding agents on your machine (`--target auto`; Claude Code if it finds none) and symlinks the skills into each one's skills folder, so a `git pull` updates them. ./install.sh --mode minimal --target claude --claude-model opus --yes                  # opus | sonnet | haiku | inherit | a model id
./install.sh --mode minimal --target opencode --opencode-model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 --yes
./install.sh --mode minimal --target codex --agent-model codex=<model-id> --yes        # any harness with file subagents

Prefer to let the agent do it? Open your agent in this folder and say **"set up papercut-explainer"**. The `papercut-setup` skill detects your agents, asks which mode and which scene-agent model you want, confirms any large download, runs the installer with the right flags and checks the result.

Install by hand: symlink or copy each folder in `skills/` into your agent's skills folder, then `export PAPERCUT_LIB="$PWD/library"`. ## Voice

Three ways to get a voice, chosen by `papercut-voice` at the start:

1. **Local Qwen3-TTS** (Full install). `library/voice/setup_tts.sh` builds a venv, downloads the model and runs a smoke test. Apple Silicon uses `mps`, NVIDIA uses `cuda`, anything else falls back to CPU, which works but takes minutes per line. Generates three takes per line, picks by ASR match and pitch movement, trims, normalises to −16 LUFS and writes word timings. On an M-series Mac the smoke test line (4 s of audio) took 40 s including model load.
2. **Your own recording, or another TTS.** Drop takes in `narration/voice/takes/narrator/<line>_<n>.wav` and run `finalize.sh` (it needs an ASR backend for word timings).
3. **Placeholder.** `python3 library/tools/placeholder_vo.py` (from the narration folder) writes silent lines, or `--say` for the macOS voice, with word times spread over each line. Build and time the whole reel first, re-voice later: the scenes key off words, so the cues follow.

Details, the `voice.json` fields and the pickers: [`library/voice/README.md`](library/voice/README.md).

Cloning a voice needs a reference clip you have the right to use.

## Customising

- **Palette and mascot.** `library/papercut/kit/tokens.ts` holds the colour roles; `hero`/`heroLo` is the critter colour. `Critter` takes colour, accessory (cap, headset, monocle…), expression and a name pill. Per-series overrides go in an episode's own `src/theme.ts`; never edit the synced `src/lib/` copy in a project.
- **Backdrops.** Drop a 1080×1920 JPEG into `library/papercut/public/bg/backdrops/`, add its name, `floorY`, mood and `bestFor` to `backdrops.json`, then run `python3 library/tools/catalog.py`. Image prompts are in `skills/papercut-explainer/references/asset-prompts.md`; the code-drawn ones are in `library/papercut/backdrops-src/`.
- **Sound.** A new effect is one file, `library/audio/sfx/<name>.js`, whose first line is `// @sfx name | tags | seconds | description | origin`. A new mood is one JSON file in `library/audio/beds/`.
- **Fonts.** `library/papercut/kit/fonts.ts` loads local woff2 files, so renders never touch the network.
- **Giving back.** After an episode, `python3 library/tools/harvest.py <project>` lists what to promote into the library (`library/HARVEST.md`); then regenerate the catalogs.

Projects keep a snapshot of the kit in `src/lib/`, so an old episode renders the same after the library changes. Re-sync with `library/papercut/sync_kit.sh <project>` when you want the new version.

## Cost

About **$14-19 in Claude API costs per 25-30 s reel**, at API list prices. Treat it as a yardstick, not a bill.

Nothing else is metered. The voice runs locally (or use the placeholder), and the 24 backdrops and all sounds ship in the repo. Make more backdrops and sounds as you need them: a backdrop is a 1080x1920 JPEG (from any image tool, or drawn in code like the sources in `library/papercut/backdrops-src/`) and a sound is one small JS file in `library/audio/sfx/`. Remotion is free for individuals and small teams (see [`THIRD_PARTY.md`](THIRD_PARTY.md)).

What moves the cost, largest first:

- **The lead session's context.** Every call re-reads the whole conversation. Start each episode in a fresh session, or compact before production starts. Strategy and research chat belong in a different session from the build.
- **Scene agents.** Fewer agents with 2-3 scenes each beat many agents with one. The bundled `papercut-scene` subagent has only file and shell tools, so each one starts small.
- **Effort level.** `high` is enough for scenes; `xhigh` costs noticeably more per scene.
- **Image reads.** Contact sheets at 200 px, one QA command per scene, two QA rounds at most.
- **Reading the kit source.** Agents read `papercut/CATALOG.md`, not the kit.

# Papercut library

A Remotion kit for short vertical (9:16) explainer reels in a cut-paper style, plus the scripts around it. The kit has paper components, 24 backdrops, camera moves, scene transitions and film-look layers. The audio folder has 79 sound effects and 8 music beds, all synthesised in code. The scripts scaffold an episode, time it to a voiceover, mix the sound, render it and pull reusable pieces back into the library.

The idea is that an episode is mostly choosing and configuring. Whoever builds it (you, or an agent following `../skills/papercut-explainer/SKILL.md`) reads two short catalogs instead of the kit source, picks sounds and a music bed by name, reuses kit components and scene templates, and writes new code only for what the episode needs that the kit lacks.

Run these from the series folder unless noted.

1. `$PAPERCUT_LIB/new_episode.sh . NN-slug CompId out-name`

4. Pick takes, fix pace and write timing: `$PAPERCUT_LIB/voice/finalize.sh voice/voice.json episodes/NN-slug/narration episodes/NN-slug/narration/voice/takes/narrator [num.json]`.
5. In `papercut/episode.json`, set `scenes` (cuts on words), `banners`, `bed`, `whipScene` and optionally `hook`. From `papercut/`, run `python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/papercut/stubs.py`, then `python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/build_vo.py`. The second command flags any scene under 1.2 s.
6. Build the first scene and `STORYBOARD.md` yourself. Give each scene agent `$PAPERCUT_LIB/papercut/AGENT_BRIEF.md` and its scene list. Each agent also writes its SFX rows to `tools/cue_sheet.d/<Scene>.json`.
7. From `papercut/`: `python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/cues.py && node $PAPERCUT_LIB/audio/render.mjs`. Check scenes with `$PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/qa.sh NAME FROM-TO NTH`, then render with `$PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/render.sh`.
8. From `papercut/`, `python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/harvest.py .` lists what the episode should give back. Promote it (`HARVEST.md`), then run `python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/catalog.py`.

## Token rules

These keep an agent's context small.

- Read `papercut/CATALOG.md` (about 60 KB) and `audio/CATALOG.md` (about 9 KB), not the kit source (about 350 KB) or the sound code. Open a source file only for one specific detail.
- Reuse before writing. A kit component, a props set (`props/council`, `props/everyday`) or a scene template (`scenes/CtaPhoneDM`) beats new drawing code. New code goes in the scene file, and anything reusable gets harvested afterwards.
- Pick SFX by name. A new sound is a new `sfx/<name>.js` file with the header line, never an edit inside a large score file.
- A music bed is a JSON preset. A new mood is a new preset.
- Beds with `"style": "night"` (`beds/night-rain-piano-F.json`) replace the plucked loop with rain on glass, room tone, a sparse felt piano and a soft pad through a convolution reverb. They also take `thinFrom`, `thinTo` and `resolveAt`. Beds without `style` render the plain loop.
- One QA command per scene, and contact sheets of at most 45 frames at 200 px, keep image tokens low.
- Each project keeps a copy of the kit (`src/lib/`), so an old episode renders the same after the library changes. Re-sync with `papercut/sync_kit.sh` when you want the new version.
